transcript.answer: After a push to main, one event can start at most three upkeep runs per repository (FR12.19a, added 2026-10-25). The pull requests upkept longest ago go first. A pull request that has never been upkept comes first. Next comes the one whose newest upkeep run started earliest, then the next oldest by that measure. Before this rule the oldest pull requests went first. That gave the same three failing pull requests on every push and deferred all the others. Pull requests left over wait for the next event.

judgements.reason: The answer states the cap of three upkeep runs per event per repository and the least-recently-upkept-first ordering: never-upkept pull requests first, then the one whose newest run started earliest. Its 'next oldest' wording loosely covers the gold's final 'then the oldest' step without contradicting it.
